[USER] User is thinking of trying a new coffee bean from Ethiopia.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ethiopian coffee is renowned for its unique flavor profile and is considered one of the best coffee-producing countries in the world.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ethiopia is the birthplace of Arabica coffee, and its high-altitude regions provide an ideal climate for coffee production.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common flavor characteristics of Ethiopian coffee include bright acidity, fruity, and floral notes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common fruit notes in Ethiopian coffee include citrus (lemon, orange), berries (strawberry, blueberry), and stone fruits (peach, apricot).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Typical floral notes found in Ethiopian coffee include rose, jasmine, and bergamot.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some Ethiopian coffees can have a tea-like quality, with hints of black tea or herbal notes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ethiopian coffee is known for its bright, snappy acidity, which adds to its lively and refreshing character.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The body of Ethiopian coffee is usually medium to light, with a clean and tea-like mouthfeel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ethiopian coffee-growing regions include Sidama, Yirgacheffe, Harrar, and Guji, each with unique flavor profiles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sidama is known for its balanced flavor, with notes of chocolate, caramel, and fruit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yirgacheffe offers a more delicate, floral, and citrusy flavor profile.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Harrar is known for its fruity, wine-like flavors and a heavier body.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Guji is known for its balanced flavor, with notes of fruit, chocolate, and a hint of spice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ethiopian coffee is often processed using natural (dry) or washed (wet) methods.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Natural processing results in a fruitier, sweeter flavor, while washed processing results in a brighter, more citrusy flavor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For brewing Ethiopian coffee, a light to medium roast is recommended to accentuate natural acidity and fruit notes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pour-over or Chemex brewing methods are suggested to allow the coffee's bright acidity and delicate flavors to shine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Experimenting with grind size is encouraged, with a medium to fine grind recommended to bring out the coffee's flavors.
